summary: We’ll never look at Valentino red the same way again. That’s the thought that came to mind stepping through the bathroom doors into Alessandro Michele’s show space, an enormous public restroom bathed in lurid red light—a gender-neutral restroom, as this was a coed show. Michele himself described the set as Lynchian, as in the late movie director David Lynch, but I saw The Shining, by Stanley Kubrick, via The Substance. This was Michele’s second ready-to-wear show for the brand. The reaction to his first was mixed, with some suggesting that the former Gucci creative director wasn’t trying hard enough to reinvent. The sound of a toilet flushing told us all we needed to know regarding how he felt about that criticism. Officially, the show was about exploring the performative nature of intimacy (hence the public-private space of the lavatory). But as one of fashion’s thought leaders on gender fluidity—Michele’s very first Gucci show gave us the men’s pussy-bow blouse—he could also have been providing a sharp commentary on the rising tide of anti-trans hate. cm-unit At a preview in Valentino’s Place Vendôme headquarters, Michele focused on the challenge of updating the house’s legacy. “It’s complicated here: You have to find a balance between contemporary maximalism and making it relevant because otherwise you risk the brand being frozen. So I’m trying to manipulate the past to make it now.” He did that by grounding the collection in a more familiar reality. Look 2’s slouchy tweed pants, V-neck sweater, and faux-fur jacket could easily slide into a street style photo gallery, and Look 8’s peekaboo bustier top and high-waist ’70s jeans wouldn’t be out of place at Caviar Kaspia late night. Michele also worked on a collaboration with Vans, but his efforts extended beyond the denim and sneakers to the show’s undone, almost work-in-progress spirit. The hems on all the pants had been let down, and models wore their hair back in knit headbands and balaclavas—no blowouts here. And then there were the bodysuits, unsnapped over lacy tights. While he made efforts to recast Valentino for the more casual lifestyles we live today, a long dress with a cat’s face, which echoed the porcelain kitty bag on last season’s runway, said that Michele’s not going to feel guilty for being himself. And for a special-occasion dress, he’s hard to top. Today’s came in silk georgette and lace in a mix of acids and pastels embellished with crystals and bows (one of those house motifs that’s hard to make look modern). There was also a striking black number with a deep plunge and a high slit, which struck a more minimal note. Valentino Garavani is a decorous man, and until his retirement in 2008, the house was associated with a jet-set politesse, high-flying but ultimately genteel. Michele is designing in more anxious, anarchic, social-mediated times. There was one thing for sure about this eccentric performance: You couldn’t look away.

mapping.note: Details matched to looks by Gemini vision inside a monotonic window, then globally aligned so parent look numbers never run backwards. Per-detail confidence and evidence are in 'detail_matches'.

detail_matches.evidence: The model's lace headwear, hair, makeup, sheer lace high-neck top, and satin bandeau undergarment are an exact match to Look 1.
The model's headscarf, hair, makeup, fur coat, striped ruffled blouse, V-neck sweater, shell necklace with gold flower pendant, and grey tweed trousers are all identical to those in the detail image.
The detail image shows a brown fur coat, grey wide-leg trousers, and a distinctive brown leather handbag with a gold chain strap and 'V' logo. Look 2 features all these exact items.

The detail shows a black structured handbag with a gold 'V' logo and key charm, black trousers, and a dark patterned jacket with black cuffs. Look 3 features the identical handbag, black trousers, and a matching dark patterned jacket.

The detail image perfectly matches Look 4, showing the same male model wearing the identical black wide-brimmed hat, black zippered turtleneck, and distinctive red coat with a wide collar and raglan sleeves.
The detail image shows a red coat, black wide-leg trousers, leopard print shoes, and a black crocodile-embossed Valentino bag. Look 4 features all these exact items.

The detail image perfectly matches Look 5 in the embroidered sheer sleeve, the fur trim on the skirt, the white floral lace tights, the black bow heels with white embroidery, and the black quilted bag with a gold chain strap and logo.

The detail image perfectly matches Look 6, including the beige lace headscarf, the dark red sunglasses with yellow lenses, the reddish-pink lace turtleneck top, the double-strand dark beaded necklace, and the light pink ruched strapless bodice with a ruffled front.

The detail image perfectly matches Look 7, including the black hat, black balaclava, blue-lensed sunglasses, cream collared coat, shell necklace with ornate pendant, and black studded shoulder bag.
The detail image perfectly matches the cream coat, black studded shoulder bag, chunky necklace, light brown trousers, and black head covering of Look 7.

The black wide-leg trousers and the distinctive red and black checkered slip-on shoes with white soles are an exact match to Look 9.

The detail image perfectly matches the model's light beige ribbed knit cap with lace trim, cream oval sunglasses with yellow lenses, and sheer lace high-neck top, including the model's facial features.
The detail image perfectly matches the blue lace top, pink ruffled peplum with black bow, teal skirt, and green sequined cuff visible in Look 11.

The detail shows a black strappy heel with rhinestone embellishments and a flared heel, along with a teal pleated fabric and patterned hosiery. Look 11 features the exact same shoes, teal pleated skirt, and patterned hosiery.

The detail image perfectly matches the distinctive zebra-print flat shoes and the dark, finely patterned trousers worn in Look 13.

The detail image perfectly matches Look 16, including the light pink knitted headband, blue sunglasses, dark blue fur-trimmed jacket, black chain-strap bag, and grey patterned trousers.
